subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: Should the Telegram plugin add a public channel/account parse or text-mode config, and which values/defaults should be supported across sends, captions, edits, and streaming previews?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but exposing parse mode changes a public config contract and affects Telegram rendering, escaping, rich-message compatibility, and security boundaries.

options.title: Add Narrow Plain/HTML Config
options.body: Preserve the current standard HTML-compatible default and add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with clear account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

options.title: Include MarkdownV2 Or Entity Modes
options.body: Support broader formatting choices, accepting a larger product and security review around MarkdownV2 escaping, raw HTML, custom emoji, and Telegram entity semantics.

options.title: Keep Existing Knobs Only
options.body: Decline a parse-mode config for now and continue improving `richMessages`, `markdown.tables`, and targeted formatter behavior instead.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Plain/HTML Config
recommendation.body: Preserve the current standard HTML-compatible default and add an explicit plain/no-parse mode with clear account inheritance and full outbound-funnel coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for the HTML-formatting decision, richMessages opt-in gate, and prior parse-mode product review context.
